newsitem.title: SYRIA: Radicals call for Holy War against Israel.
newsitem.headline: Radicals call for Holy War against Israel.

text.p: Three radical Palestinian groups on Wednesday called on Palestinians to launch Jihad (Holy War) and military attacks against Israel to force it to stop building a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

The call was made in separate statements issued in Damascus by the Islamic Jihad group, the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP) and the Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine (DFLP). The groups have claimed several attacks in which scores of Israelis were killed.

"It is time for Jihad. It is time to launch all types of resistance against Israel. It is time to teach the Zionist enemy that Jerusalem is ours and we will not abandon an atom of its soil," the Islamic Jihad said in its statement.

"To all children, women and old men in the occupied territories: Jerusalem is calling upon you to confront with your bodies the Israeli bulldozers which are smashing the bones of our ancestors," it said.

The Islamic Jihad, which opposes Israel's 1993 peace deal with the PLO, accused Palestinian President Yasser Arafat of making a sell-out deal with Israel through which it allows his plane to land at the Palestinian airport in Gaza in return for keeping silent about the new settlement.
"Arafat is seeking a cheap deal through which he exchanges Holy Jerusalem with a permission to allow his plane to land at the Gaza airport," the Jihad statement said.

The calls were made as Israeli bulldozers ripped into Jebel Abu Ghneim, or Har Homa as called by Israel, in the disputed city for the second day to build 6,500 houses for Jews despite international condemnation.
Arab countries -- along with many European nations and the United States -- have criticised the construction and warned that this could lead to violence.

The plan aims at completing a ring of Jewish neighbourhoods around East Jerusalem that would cement Israel's claim to the city as Israel's "eternal, undivided" capital. Palestinians regard East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state.
Maher al-Taher, spokesman for the Marxist PFLP led by George Habash, urged "all Palestinians to confront the Israeli bulldozers and to prevent the building of the new Jewish settlement."

"The Israeli plan constitutes a flagrant and dangerous challenge to the will of the Arab nation, Moslems, Christians and the whole world. It requires a quick and practical response and not only statements of condemnation," Taher said.
"Escalation of the military confrontation is the only language that Israel understands. It is the language which should be used against (Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu's government," he said.
The PFLP spokesman condemned calls by Arafat for calm, saying confrontation was the only means to stop Netanyahu's plans.
"The PFLP will continue its struggle and will confront occupation and settlements with all means," Taher said.
He called for an urgent Arab summit to discuss the Israeli plans and to adopt action that would prevent Israel from continuing its building process.
Ali Badwan, spokesman for the DFLP led by Nayef Hawatmeh, said the building of a new settlement in East Jerusalem "would put the region over a barrel of explosives."
"We call upon all Palestinian factions to unify their ranks to escalate all types of fighting against Israel and the Jewish settlers," he said.
Syria and Egypt on Wednesday accused Israel of leading the region into a new era of violence and war by building the controversial Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem.
